Key Takeaway

A full-service direct mail campaign from Cornerstone includes everything: mailing list targeting, mail piece design, commercial printing, address verification, USPS presort, and post office delivery — all from one facility in New Paltz, NY. No vendors, no handoffs. A typical 5,000-piece postcard campaign runs $0.65–$0.90 per piece all-in and delivers in 7–10 business days.

What's Included in a Full Direct Mail Campaign

A direct mail campaign with Cornerstone starts with your mailing list and ends at the mailbox. Every step happens at our New Paltz, NY production facility — no outsourcing, no third-party vendors, no handoffs. Here is what is included in every full-service campaign:

Mailing List Targeting and Data Hygiene

Consumer and business lists filtered by geography, demographics, homeownership, income, SIC code, length of residence, or any combination of selects relevant to your audience. We pull from compiled data sources covering 140+ million US households. Every list — whether you provide it or we build it — runs through CASS/DPV address verification and NCOA processing before a single piece prints. CASS corrects and standardizes addresses. DPV confirms each address actually receives mail. NCOA catches anyone who has filed a change of address in the past 48 months. The result is a clean, deliverable list that qualifies for the lowest USPS automation postage rates.

Mail Piece Design

USPS-compliant design for every format we produce: postcards (4×6, 6×9, 6×11), letters with window or closed-face envelopes, self-mailers, brochures, and newsletters. Our design team builds mail pieces for response — readable headline in three seconds, clear call to action, correct USPS indicia placement, and Intelligent Mail barcode formatting. If you supply print-ready artwork, we go straight to production. If you need design, we handle it in-house.

Commercial Printing

In-house production presses for postcards, letters, self-mailers, and newsletters. We print full-color on both sides, run inkjet addressing directly on the piece, and apply Intelligent Mail barcodes for USPS automation compatibility. Print-to-induction turnaround for a standard postcard is 3–5 business days from approved proof. Letters and self-mailers run 4–7 business days. No print broker, no gang-run wait times — we control the press schedule.

Presort and USPS Preparation

Every mailing is sorted to USPS automation standards and presented for the lowest applicable postage rate. Marketing Mail presort runs $0.22–$0.30 per piece depending on piece size and sortation level. We hold a USPS Business Mail Entry Unit permit — you do not need your own. Presort discounts kick in at 200 pieces. Most campaigns run 1,000+ pieces, which qualifies for full automation pricing.

USPS Induction and Delivery Tracking

We truck finished mailings directly to the post office and induct at the Business Mail Entry Unit. No drops at retail counters, no postage meter delays. You receive USPS Informed Visibility tracking data confirming when your mail entered the postal stream and when it arrived at the destination Sectional Center Facility. For targeted direct mail campaigns, we can also set up USPS Informed Delivery coordination — adding a digital email preview of your piece to subscribers' morning inbox the day it arrives. Informed Delivery averages a 63% open rate, compared to 20% for typical email marketing.

EDDM vs. Targeted Direct Mail: Which Fits Your Campaign?

Every Door Direct Mail (EDDM) saturates every address on a USPS carrier route. No list required, no permit needed for retail EDDM, and postage runs $0.22–$0.23 per piece — the lowest available rate. It's the right tool when geographic reach matters more than demographic precision: a restaurant opening, a home services company blanketing a new service area, a political campaign covering a precinct.

Targeted direct mail uses a purchased or house list filtered by demographics, geography, purchase behavior, or any combination of selects that narrows the audience to likely buyers. Higher cost per piece — typically $0.65–$0.90 all-in — but higher response rates because you are mailing to people who already match your buyer profile. It's the right tool for customer acquisition, reactivation, and high-value offer campaigns.

Cornerstone runs both. We recommend the right approach based on your campaign goals, budget, and target geography. Many clients run a combination — EDDM for broad awareness and targeted mail for customer acquisition. Read our complete EDDM guide for a detailed breakdown of how EDDM campaigns work.

What to Expect: Direct Mail Response Rates

The Data & Marketing Association puts the average direct mail response rate at 4.4% for house lists and 2.9% for prospect lists — compared to 0.12% for email. For a 5,000-piece campaign at 2% response, that is 100 leads. At a $300 average transaction and a 25% close rate, those 100 leads become $7,500 in revenue from a $4,000 campaign. The metric that matters is not cost-per-piece — it is cost-per-response.

Five factors drive response rate more than anything else: list quality (who you are mailing to), offer strength (what you are offering), mail piece format (postcard vs. letter), timing (when it arrives), and frequency (how many times you mail). We help you optimize all five. For more on how direct mail stacks up against digital channels, see our direct mail vs. email marketing comparison.

How Long Does a Direct Mail Campaign Take?

Standard turnaround at Cornerstone is 7–10 business days from approved proof to post office induction. USPS Marketing Mail then delivers in 3–5 business days for local Hudson Valley mailings in Ulster, Dutchess, and Orange counties — 7–10 days for national campaigns. Total time from kick-off to in-home: plan for 15–20 business days if starting from scratch.

For established clients with pre-approved templates and a clean list, 10–12 business days is achievable. Rush production is available when the schedule allows — call to confirm availability. Election mail and time-sensitive campaigns get priority scheduling. For more detail on how mail automation specs affect turnaround, see our Notice 67 reference.

Direct Mail for Real Estate Agents in the Hudson Valley

Real estate farming is one of the highest-ROI applications of direct mail. The agents who show up in the mailbox every 4–6 weeks with relevant local information become the default call when a homeowner in that area decides to sell. A targeted homeowner list by carrier route, filtered to suppress renters and target length-of-residence of five years or more, gives you the audience most likely to be sellers.

Most successful real estate farming programs mail 8–12 times per year to 500–1,000 households per farm area. A 6×11 postcard at that volume runs approximately $0.70–$0.85 per piece including design, printing, list processing, and postage. The agents who commit to consistent mailing for 12+ months see compounding results — response rates increase with frequency because recognition and trust build over repeated exposure.

How Much Does Direct Mail Cost?

A standard 6×9 postcard campaign at 5,000 pieces runs $0.65–$0.90 per piece all-in — that includes design, printing, list processing, presort, and postage. Letters run $0.80–$1.10 per piece at the same quantity. Volume breaks matter: cost at 10,000 pieces runs 20–25% lower per piece than at 1,000 pieces due to print gang pricing and deeper presort discounts.

The number that matters is cost-per-response, not cost-per-piece. At 2% response on 5,000 pieces, you have 100 leads. If 25% of those close at a $300 average transaction, that's $7,500 in revenue. The cost of the campaign — $3,250–$4,500 all-in — pays back within one cycle for most local businesses. Not sure about budget? Use our direct mail cost calculator to estimate printing, postage, and design costs. Request a free itemized estimate to see exact pricing for your campaign.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much does a direct mail campaign cost?

A 6×9 postcard campaign at 5,000 pieces runs $0.65–$0.90 per piece all-in, including design, printing, list processing, and postage. Letters run $0.80–$1.10 at the same quantity. Larger quantities lower the per-piece cost significantly — 10,000 pieces typically runs 20–25% less per piece than 1,000 pieces. Get a free itemized estimate within one business day.

What is the difference between EDDM and targeted direct mail?

Every Door Direct Mail (EDDM) delivers to every address on a USPS carrier route — no list needed, postage runs $0.22–$0.23 per piece. Targeted direct mail uses a purchased or house list filtered by demographics or geography — higher cost per piece, typically $0.65–$0.90 all-in, but higher response rates because you are mailing to people who match your buyer profile. We run both and will recommend the right approach for your campaign goals.

How long does a direct mail campaign take?

Standard turnaround at Cornerstone is 7–10 business days from approved proof to post office induction. USPS Marketing Mail then delivers in 3–5 business days for local Hudson Valley mailings. Total time from kick-off to in-home: plan for 15–20 business days if starting from scratch. Rush production is available for established clients — call to confirm availability.

What response rate should I expect?

The Data & Marketing Association reports a 4.4% average response rate for house lists and 2.9% for prospect lists. For a first campaign to a cold list, 1–2% is a realistic baseline. Rates improve with list quality, offer testing, and repeated mailings to the same list. Direct mail consistently outperforms email (0.12% average response) for local response.

Do you outsource any part of the job?

No. Data, design, printing, addressing, presorting, and USPS induction all happen at our facility in New Paltz, NY. One team, one building, no handoffs. When we give you a turnaround commitment, we own it.

What is the minimum quantity for a direct mail campaign?

There is no hard minimum. Presort automation discounts start at 200 pieces. Most campaigns run 1,000+ pieces to achieve meaningful response data and cost-efficient presort rates. Very small quantities — under 200 pieces — mail at First Class rates without presort discounts.

Do you offer USPS Informed Delivery coordination?

Yes. Informed Delivery sends subscribers a digital email preview of your mail piece the morning it arrives — average open rate 63%, versus 20% for typical email marketing. We handle coordinated campaign setup including ride-along image creation and USPS Business Portal submission. Available for targeted direct mail; not available for EDDM campaigns. Ask about it when you request your estimate.

Do you offer nonprofit mailing rates?

Yes. Organizations that qualify for Nonprofit Marketing Mail rates can mail at significantly lower postage rates than standard Marketing Mail. Cornerstone holds a nonprofit mailing authorization and can process qualifying mailings at the nonprofit rate. Contact us to confirm eligibility — we will review your organization type and help with the authorization if needed.
